cards.q: What is an MPLS label and where is it carried?
cards.a: MPLS forwarding is driven by labels, which are 20-bit values carried in a 32-bit shim header between L2 and L3. Each router swaps the top label and forwards, and a packet can carry a label stack of multiple shims for VPNs and TE tunnels.

cards.q: What are the four fields of the 32-bit MPLS shim header and their bit sizes?
cards.a: Label (20 bits, forwarding value), Exp (3 bits, QoS/class), S (1 bit, bottom-of-stack), and TTL (8 bits, hop limit).

cards.q: Which field of the shim header drives the swap and which marks the bottom of the stack?
cards.a: The Label field drives the swap; the S (bottom-of-stack) bit marks the last label. Exp marks class and TTL limits loops.

cards.q: What are the reserved MPLS label value ranges?
cards.a: 0-15 are reserved (special), 16-1023 are explicit null and others, and 16-1,048,575 are normal labels.

cards.q: How is a label stack structured for VPN traffic?
cards.a: The top label forwards in the core (transport), the inner label is the service (VPN) label, and the bottom (S=1) is the deepest. VPN uses two labels: transport plus service.

cards.q: What do push, swap, and pop operations do to a label stack?
cards.a: Push adds a label, swap changes the top label, and pop removes it.

cards.q: Where does each label operation occur: push, swap, pop?
cards.a: Push occurs on the ingress LER (adds shim), swap on the core LSR (replaces top), and pop on penultimate or egress (removes).
PHP removes the label one hop early, at the penultimate router, improving egress performance.

cards.q: What are the implicit null, explicit null, and router alert label values and their uses?
cards.a: Implicit null is label 3, used for PHP (pop before egress); explicit null is label 0, used to keep QoS (Exp) at egress; router alert is label 1, used for control traffic.

cards.q: Why would the egress use an explicit null label rather than implicit null?
cards.a: Explicit null (label 0) lets the egress still read the Exp field for QoS, whereas implicit null pops the label before the egress.

cards.q: What is the difference between pipe mode and uniform mode TTL handling?
cards.a: In pipe mode, the TTL is not decremented, hiding the core hops; in uniform mode, the TTL decrements normally. Pipe mode is used in SP networks.

cards.q: What command shows the range of labels a router can allocate?
How many bits are in each field of the shim header?
cards.a: Label 20 bits, Exp 3 bits, S 1 bit, and TTL 8 bits, totalling 32 bits.

cards.q: What are the values of implicit null, explicit null, and how many labels does VPN carry?
cards.a: Implicit null is 3, explicit null is 0, and VPN uses a two-label stack (transport + service). PHP pops early.
